summary: PickPath auto-picker prefers Fleet over Hermes for ClassOwnerAPI, gated by a fail-closed dispatch-readiness predicate plus a live-call auth backstop; Hermes is the fallback when Fleet is not provably ready, fails auth at send time, or on explicit --via=hermes.
reason: Fleet handles all signed commands reliably from anywhere, but via=auto must be fail-closed: Fleet is picked only with a resolvable signing key, tesla-control on PATH, and credential evidence (future JWT exp, recorded future expiry, or a mintable refresh grant: refresh token + client ID); a nonempty token string alone is never evidence. Revocation and signature validity are unknowable offline, so dispatch adds the live backstop: refresh-only configs mint before dispatch, and via=auto owner-API commands reroute to a running Hermes relay whenever Fleet cannot authenticate at send time (failed initial mint, or a 401 persisting after the bounded refresh retry). Explicit --via=fleet always attempts Fleet and errors specifically, never rerouting.
validated_outcome: Valid-token+key+binary -> Fleet; expired-JWT-env-var+no-refresh+hermesRunning -> Hermes fallback; --via=fleet always tries Fleet
